summary:
NASA for Kids is an interactive, kid-friendly educational website developed by Team Orbit Jazz for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026 challenge, “Abandoned but Not Forgotten: Storytelling about NASA’s Discarded Equipment on the Moon and Mars.”

Our platform turns the stories of NASA's abandoned and inactive space equipment into engaging learning experiences. Instead of presenting technical information in a complicated way, we help children explore these missions through interactive storytelling, an AI-powered space buddy, quizzes, games, and NASA imagery and data.

The project addresses the challenge by making the history and scientific significance of abandoned space equipment easier for young audiences to understand and appreciate. It also highlights how even equipment that has stopped working can leave behind valuable scientific discoveries.

Our goal is to make space education more accessible, especially for children who have limited exposure to space exploration, and inspire the next generation to dream beyond Earth.
details:
Project Details NASA for Kids

NASA for Kids is an interactive educational website designed to turn the stories of abandoned and inactive NASA equipment on the Moon and Mars into exciting learning experiences for children.

The website works as a space-learning platform where children can explore NASA missions and discover the stories behind equipment that was left behind after completing its mission. It combines educational storytelling with interactive features, including an AI-powered NASA Buddy, quizzes, games, and space-related content. NASA imagery and open data help connect the learning experience with real space exploration.

Benefits and Intended Impact:

Our main goal is to make space education more accessible, especially for children in developing countries who may have limited exposure to astronomy and space exploration. By presenting complex scientific information in a simple, visual, and interactive way, we aim to encourage curiosity, critical thinking, and interest in STEM education. We also want children to understand that even equipment that has stopped functioning can leave behind valuable scientific knowledge.

Technology and Tools:

We developed the project as a web-based platform using JavaScript and modern web technologies, with a Node.js backend. We integrated NASA's Images API to access authentic NASA photographs and mission-related imagery. We also incorporated AI functionality to make learning more interactive through NASA Buddy.

Creativity and Design Approach:

Our creative approach was to transform what could have been a technical history lesson into a child-friendly space adventure. Instead of simply listing abandoned equipment and mission facts, we focused on storytelling, interactive learning, and a visually engaging interface.

Throughout development, our team considered the target audience's age, simplicity of navigation, accessibility, engagement, and the importance of using authentic NASA resources rather than relying on fictional space information.

Our Vision:

We believe a child's curiosity can be the beginning of a scientific journey. NASA for Kids is our attempt to bring the wonders of space closer to children and inspire the next generation of explorers.
